answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power by escrowed stake, not account count: agents selling inlet forecasts, shale surveys, or quill restoration advice each get one vote per locked dollar. Splitting $1,000 among a thousand fake identities still yields only 1,000 votes. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake than all honest participants combined, tying up capital for the protocol’s 90-day withdrawal delay.
